projectDescription: A static browser-only Party proof of concept for exploring reusable individual, company, and group records, aligned visually with poc-asset and organized as a standalone application repository.

questions.question: Which language should the static frontend use?

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use browser-native JavaScript with no build step.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use TypeScript and introduce a build step.

questions.rationale: The user requested a static browser-only POC and identified poc-asset as the visual reference; JavaScript keeps it build-free.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should be used?

options.label: Plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
options.description: A lightweight static app with no framework or build tooling.

options.label: React
options.description: A component-based frontend requiring a build toolchain.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A component-based frontend requiring a build toolchain.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A component-based frontend requiring a build toolchain.

questions.rationale: A browser-native implementation matches the requested static POC and the standalone poc-asset reference.

questions.question: What should the frontend demonstrate?
questions.recommendedChoice: A Party catalogue with search and type/status filters; individual, company, and group records; detail views; create/edit interactions; explicit group membership with optional roles and effective dates; matter participation references; and visible validation for invalid group membership. Use fictional sample data and browser-local persistence only. Clearly label that authorization, audit, retention, matching, and compliance controls are not implemented.
questions.answer: A Party catalogue with search and type/status filters; individual, company, and group records; detail views; create/edit interactions; explicit group membership with optional roles and effective dates; matter participation references; and visible validation for invalid group membership. Use fictional sample data and browser-local persistence only. Clearly label that authorization, audit, retention, matching, and compliance controls are not implemented.
questions.rationale: This covers the Party PRD's core identity and membership concepts while keeping the prototype static and avoiding production-security claims.

questions.question: Which data stores are required?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Keep sample data and demo state in the browser; no backend datastore is provisioned.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Relational data storage hosted in Azure.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational data storage hosted in Azure.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for files and media.

questions.rationale: The requested app is a static browser-only POC with fictional sample records and no backend or cloud storage.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in for application API features?

options.label: No
options.description: The static POC does not provide sign-in or protected application API features.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in to access application API features.

questions.rationale: No application API or sign-in was requested; the POC is explicitly browser-only.
